newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says Eisai cut not due to negative factors. [CORRECTED 02:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Nomura says Eisai cut not due to negative factors. [CORRECTED 02:25 GMT]

text.p: Nomura Research Institute Ltd's downgrading of Eisai Co Ltd on Tuesday was not (corrects) done as a result of negative factors for the drug firm, Nomura Securities Co Ltd said.

The research institute, an arm of Nomura Securities, downgraded the pharmaceuticals maker earlier on Tuesday because the impact of approval for its new Alzheimer's drug had already been factored into its share price, the securities house said.
There are no fresh negative factors to affect the company's fundamentals, Nomura Research officials were quoted by the brokerage as saying.
Nomura Research downgraded Eisai to a "2" rating from its previous "1", market sources said.

In its three-grade rating system, the research institute assigns a "2" rating to issues whose values it sees moving within 10 percentage points in either direction of the key 225-share Nikkei average over the next six months.

Eisai said in November that its U.S. subsidiary, Eisai America Inc, received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its drug Aricept, which is for mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease, in the United States.
Eisai shares fell on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Tuesday morning after Nomura Research's downgrading.
By 0200 GMT, Eisai shares fell 70 yen to 2,210.
